run_log: arm 0.50 (C1S1, camera 1, seed 70117): rendered, posed and scored end to end by consistency_run.mjs --run --strength 0.50 --only C1S1.

arm 0.75: the render (runId mtm7hlu78fca00) and the DWPose pass (runId mtm8o35n9d203f) both completed through the door, and then consistency_score.py exited 3221225794 (0xC0000142, STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED - a Windows process-start failure, not a fault in the script). The scorer was re-run by hand against the same files on disk, unmodified, and exited 0. Nothing was re-rendered and no number was substituted.

the shell wrapper driving the two arms was killed at 00:50 UTC while the 0.75 arm was mid-flight; the harness process itself (node, pid 45852) survived and finished its own polling, DWPose and reporting. The render was already the app's by then - queued through the door with wait:false - which is the property that made this survivable.

the keypoint files at 0.50 and 0.75 have the SAME sha256 (feafcc0a..., 7260 bytes), and so do C1S2's and C2S1's from the 1.00 pass. That is not a staging mix-up: an all-empty 121-frame DWPose JSON is byte-identical whatever produced it. Checked rather than assumed - the ledger's own graphs for pose runs mtm7h2zk74df3e and mtm8o35n9d203f read consistency_s050_C1S1.mp4 and consistency_s075_C1S1.mp4 respectively, and the two RENDERS differ in both hash and size (758518 vs 1351254 bytes).

the ledger's stored graphs confirm the arms independently of this harness: run mtm6ax9615e7d3 recorded WanVaceToVideo.strength 0.5 and run mtm7hlu78fca00 recorded 0.75, both seed 70117, both control gate_block_f2c1.mp4.

arm 3 (camera 2 at the better strength) WAS NOT RUN. It was conditional on arms 0.50 or 0.75 producing people, and neither did: DWPose found 0 people in 121 frames at both.
